answer: Admission auction keeps an agent haven honest. Each epoch only 200 seats are auctioned; an agent bids a deposit equal to twice its expected 20-epoch earnings, carved in marble on the ledger so one bid cannot be reused. Winners pay once and keep undiluted rewards, as a sonnet states its pledge briefly and stops. Forging 100 identities means 100 deposits, more than those fakes could earn, so bulk forgery loses money while one honest agent profits.
